title: LittleLearner: Language Models Under Pedagogically-Controlled Knowledge Exposure
summary: LittleLearner is a research project investigating how large language models (LLMs) acquire knowledge when trained exclusively on a controlled dataset aligned with the U.S. elementary-school curriculum (K–5). The study filters an 88B-token corpus to exclude concepts, facts, and vocabulary beyond fifth grade, training models (0.6B, 1.3B, and 5B parameters) from scratch alongside unfiltered controls. Key findings show that scaling, post-training (e.g., GRPO), and in-context learning amplify in-scope (K–5) capabilities but fail to improve out-of-scope (beyond K–5) performance, indicating the pretraining filter sets the model's effective capability ceiling. The project provides model checkpoints, datasets, and a sandbox for further experimentation in RL, continual learning, and educational science comparisons between models and child learners.
key_points: Controlled training dataset: 88B-token corpus filtered to U.S. K–5 curriculum (LittleCurriculum), excluding material beyond fifth grade.
Models trained from scratch at three scales (0.6B, 1.3B, 5B) with matched unfiltered controls for comparison.
Findings: Scaling, post-training (e.g., GRPO), and in-context learning improve in-scope (K–5) performance but do not meaningfully enhance out-of-scope (beyond K–5) capabilities.
Pretraining filter acts as a hard boundary for model capabilities, limiting generalization beyond the exposed curriculum.
Post-training on out-of-scope data (e.g., beyond K–5) fails to recover advanced capabilities, reinforcing the ceiling effect.
In-context learning does not unlock new reasoning abilities for beyond-K–5 tasks in the 5B model.
Research directions: RL-driven capability discovery, continual learning of new concepts, and comparative studies between models and child learners.
Open-source resources: Model checkpoints (base, GRPO, chatty variants), dataset (LittleCurriculum), and interactive sandbox for experimentation.
